[[Doctor]] '''Crell Moset''' was a [[male]] [[Cardassian]] [[exobiologist]] of the [[24th century]] [[Cardassian Union]]. By [[2371]], he became the [[chief exobiology specialist]] on [[Cardassia Prime]] and was the [[Chairman of Exobiology]] at the [[University of Culat]]. He was renowned even among other civilizations as the foremost [[exobiologist]] who specialized in [[non-humanoid exobiology]]. To all outward appearances, Moset was polite and courteous with a brilliant medical mind. But, in reality, Crell Moset, was cold, calculating and ruthless; doing whatever he wanted to get the data he needed.

During the [[Occupation of Bajor]], Dr. Moset was practicing medicine on [[Bajor]]. Without the resources to try traditional methods, Moset experimented with procedures that never would have occurred to him under ordinary circumstances. As a doctor on Bajor, Moset found the simplest tools, such as [[scalpel]]s, were the most effective because modern equipment removed a doctor from his subject. It was by these methods that he accidentally discovered the cure for the [[Fostossa virus]] epidemic, saving thousands of Bajorans' lives and for which he won the [[Legate's Crest of Valor]]. 

[[File:Crell Mosets laboratory.jpg|thumb|left|Crell Moset's lab]]
What was unknown outside of [[Cardassia]] and Bajor, however, was the fact that all of Moset's experiments were performed on living people. Thousands of Bajorans were killed in his so-called hospital, including {{USS|Voyager}} crewmember [[Ensign]] [[Tabor]]'s [[Tabor's brother 001|brother]] and [[Tabor's grandfather 001|grandfather]]. Many of his studies included experiments such as blinding his "patients" so he could study how they adapted, or exposing them to [[polytrinic acid]] just to see how long it would take for their [[skin]] to heal. 

The most horrific part of Moset's experiments was the method used to cure the Fostossa virus epidemic, which was accomplished by infecting hundreds of people so that he could experiment with different treatments. According to [[Starfleet]] records, Moset purchased many biochemical agents, including every known {{dis|strain|biology}} of the Fostossa virus – a typical procedure in the development of [[vaccine]]s. However, he didn't ask for any of the [[enzyme]]s normally required for synthesizing a vaccine. Four days after he received the virus samples, there was a minor outbreak of Fostossa in the vicinity of his hospital. Prior to that date, there had not been a single case in the entire [[province]]. 

In [[2375]], Dr. Moset's data was consulted by [[The Doctor]] aboard ''Voyager'' in an effort to remove a [[cytoplasmic lifeform]] that was living on [[Lt.]] [[B'Elanna Torres]]. B'Elanna and others vehemently objected to the use of Moset's knowledge to treat B'Elanna, considering Moset a war criminal. The Doctor, meanwhile, expressed his desire to save B'Elanna regardless of Moset's professional history. Considering him a genius (but lacking knowledge of the atrocities he had committed), The Doctor even made a holographic simulation of Dr. Moset as "''[[Medical Consultant Program Beta one]]''". The Doctor deleted the hologram after the creature had been removed as he was unable to reconcile Moset's successes with the brutal methods he resorted to in order to gain the data in the first place. ({{VOY|Nothing Human}})

== Appendices ==
=== Background information ===
Moset was played by actor [[David Clennon]].

===Apocrypha===
In the novel ''[[The Battle of Betazed]]'', Crell Moset experiments on the [[Betazoid]]s after the [[Dominion]] [[Battle of Betazed|conquers]] the planet, hoping to create [[telepath]]ic [[Jem'Hadar]], only for the experiment to fail when the Jem'Hadar prove incapable of coping with the increased sensory input. Moset also appeared in the ''Voyager'' Relaunch ''[[Star Trek: Voyager - Spirit Walk|Spirit Walk]]'' novels, where he is rescued from Starfleet capture by a renegade [[Changeling]] who became trapped in Solid form several years ago and seeks Moset's help in restoring his old abilities, simultaneously experimenting on [[Chakotay]]'s people to unlock the full potential of their [[Sky Spirit]]-enhanced DNA. At the conclusion, Moset is confronted by ''Voyager''{{'}}s new doctor Jarem Kaz, a [[Trill]] whose previous host's wife was killed by Moset's experiments, who coldly forced Moset to realize just how horrific and evil he would be regarded as by future generations, subsequently refusing to kill him as he preferred to leave Moset forced to look at a mirror of just how ruthless he was.

In the ''[[Star Trek: Terok Nor]]'' novel ''[[Night of the Wolves]]'', Moset infected [[Kira Nerys]]' mother [[Kira Meru]] with the Fostossa virus in [[2353]] on the orders of [[Gul]] [[Dukat]], who believed that she was becoming a liability. Meru died shortly thereafter.

His [[mirror universe]] {{mb|Crell Moset (mirror)|counterpart}} appears in the novella ''[[The Mirror-Scaled Serpent]]'' and the short story "Bitter Fruit" contained in the anthology ''[[Shards and Shadows]]''. He is described as performing experiments similar to those conducted by his primary universe counterpart on {{mu|Terran}}s and others species on behalf of the [[Klingon-Cardassian Alliance]].

{{sidebar individual |image = Mila, 2375.jpg |caption = Mila (2375) |affiliation = [[Cardassian Liberation Front]] |species = [[Cardassian]] |occupation = [[Housekeeper]] |status = [[Deceased]]; killed by the [[Jem'Hadar]] |datestatus = 2375 |died = 2375,
[[Cardassia Prime]] |actor = [[Julianna McCarthy]] |image2 = Mila, 2371.jpg |caption2 = Mila (2371) }} {{aquote|I was never much of a [[cook]], but I knew how to keep a [[secret]].|Mila|2375|The Dogs of War}} '''Mila''' was a [[female]] [[Cardassian]] who lived during the late [[24th century]]. == History == Mila was employed as the [[housekeeper]] of former [[Obsidian Order]] head [[Enabran Tain]] for over [[2330s|thirty years]]. Over that time, she was Tain's closest [[confidante]], since even though she "wasn't much of a [[cook]]", she knew how to keep [[secret]]s. Mila was fond of Tain's son, [[Elim Garak]], whom she practically raised as her own [[child]]. Mila always firmly believed that Garak was innocent of Tain's allegations of betrayal. In [[2371]], Garak contacted Mila for the first time since his [[exile]], concerning Tain's whereabouts after the deaths of several former Obsidian Order [[agent]]s. Mila informed him that Tain had departed in a hurry, and pleaded with Garak to help him. ({{DS9|Improbable Cause}}) When Garak and Tain reunited, Tain idly considered [[execution|executing]] Mila as she knew "too much for her own good." Garak objected, rationalizing that she was both trustworthy and a capable housekeeper. In truth, he was as fond of her as she was of him. ({{DS9|The Die is Cast}}) Mila saw Garak again during the [[Dominion War]] in [[2375]] before her death. Garak, [[Damar]], and [[Kira Nerys]] were stranded on [[Cardassia Prime]] when the [[Cardassian Liberation Front]] was wiped out by the [[Dominion]]. Mila sheltered them in the [[basement]] of Tain's house, from which they organized a new civilian resistance movement. ({{DS9|The Dogs of War}}) During a [[power outage]], the resistance fighters were discovered as enemy [[Jem'Hadar]] soldiers were searching the city for them. Mila answered the door, and tried to send the soldiers away, but they were determined. She was killed and her body was thrown down the basement stairs before they stormed in. Garak promptly swore revenge for Mila's death. ({{DS9|What You Leave Behind}}) == Appendices == === Appearances === * {{DS9}} ** {{e|Improbable Cause}} ** {{e|The Dogs of War}} ** {{e|What You Leave Behind}} === Background information === Mila was played by [[Julianna McCarthy]]. According to the {{st-minutiae|resources/scripts/467.txt|script}} for "The Die is Cast", Mila was pronounced as "MEE-lah". === Apocrypha === The {{s|DS9}} {{novel}} ''[[A Stitch in Time]]'' reveals that Mila was indeed [[Garak's mother 001|Garak's mother]], however, he was raised believing his father was a man named Tolan rather than Tain. Shortly before his own death, Tolan told Garak the truth about his parentage. After Tolan had died, Mila explained to Garak that Tolan was her brother. === External links === * {{mbeta|Mila Garak}} [[de:Mila]] [[es:Mila]] [[Category:Cardassians]]

{{sidebar individual |image = Makbar.jpg |caption = Makbar in 2370 |species = [[Cardassian]] |occupation = [[Chief Archon]] |status = Active |datestatus = 2370 |actor = [[Caroline Lagerfelt]] }} '''Makbar''' was a [[Cardassian]] [[female]] who served as a [[Chief Archon]] on [[Cardassia Prime]] during the late-[[24th century]]. == History == In [[2370]], she presided over [[Miles O'Brien]]'s trial for smuggling [[weapon]]s to the [[Maquis]]. In fact, Makbar was part of an elaborate scheme to attempt to discredit the [[Federation]]'s [[policy|policies]] and to establish grounds to invade the [[Demilitarized Zone|DMZ]] to eliminate the Maquis. They attempted to portray the Maquis as "savage, Federation-born killers" who were operating with secret but official sanction from [[Starfleet Command]]. The plot failed when [[Commander]] [[Benjamin Sisko|Sisko]] discovered that it was a {{dis|Raymond Boone|Cardassian| Cardassian agent}} disguised as [[Raymond Boone]] who used O'Brien's recorded voice to [[steal]] the weapons from [[Deep Space 9]]. Makbar immediately recognized the ersatz Boone when he was brought in, along with the unspoken threat from Sisko he would publicly expose the plan if O'Brien were convicted, embarrassing [[Cardassian Central Command]] in front of all Cardassia, and potentially risking a new conflict with the Federation. She quickly declared that O'Brien, though "guilty", would be released into Federation custody in the spirit of improving Federation-Cardassian relations, thus indicating she was part of the plot and acted so that it would not be publicly exposed. ({{DS9|Tribunal}}) == Memorable quotes == "''Mrs O'Brien, there's nothing for you to prepare. Your husband's verdict has already been determined. He is guilty. The trial will reveal how this guilt was proven by the most efficient criminal investigation system in the quadrant.''" :- '''Makbar''', to Keiko O'Brien "''Mr O'Brien is being treated with great care and respect.''"
"''Good, because if he is not, I will hold you ''personally'' responsible. And if that sounds like a threat, it is.''"
"''[[Gul]] [[Dukat]]'s told me about you. You live up to your reputation, Commander.''"
"''That's right. I do.''"
:- '''Makbar''' and '''Benjamin Sisko''' "''His execution is scheduled for next week.''"
"''How can you schedule an execution before the trial even begins?''"
"''We believe in swift justice.''"
:- '''Makbar''' and '''Keiko O'Brien''' "''The offender, Miles O'Brien, Human, officer of the Federation Starfleet has been found guilty of aiding and abetting seditious acts against the state. The sentence is death. Let the trial begin.''"
:- '''Makbar''', introducing '''Miles O'Brien'''{{'}}s trial "''Gul Evek has tied the Maquis to this plot by quoting reliable sources. I think we deserve to know who these reliable sources are.''"
"''Can you provide any details, Gul Evek?''"
"''I'm afraid that information cannot be revealed without risk to national security, Madame Archon.''"
"''That's an acceptable answer.''"
:- '''Odo''', '''Makbar''' and '''Evek''' "''Once again the Cardassian system of jurisprudence has worked to protect its people. A guilty man has been brought to justice. But, never let it be said that there is no room in this system for compassion. I sense in Mister O'Brien, a man with strong family ties, the potential for rehabilitation. And I'm sure he has gained a new appreciation of [[Cardassian law]] through this difficult process. Therefore, I am pleased, in the spirit of furthering Cardassian-Federation relations, to hereby set aside the verdict and to release Mister O'Brien into the custody of his Commander, Benjamin Sisko.''" :- '''Makbar''', after the plot to discredit the Federation is revealed == Appendices == === Background information === Makbar was played by actress [[Caroline Lagerfelt]]. The final draft script for "Tribunal" gave the pronunciation of Makbar's name as "MOCK-bahr" and went on to describe her as simply "a Cardassian woman". {{st-minutiae|resources/scripts/445.txt}} The character was used to personify the cold, even grinding, philosophy of the Cardassian judicial system. In her hairstyle, hair department head [[Josée Normand]] incorporated some of the unique design details from the Cardassian courtroom. "''It was one of those times that I went over to the set for inspiration,''" she said. ({{ds9c|149|150|&}}) Two of the costumes worn by Lagerfelt as Makbar were later sold off in the [[It's A Wrap! sale and auction]]. The first, a royal blue, velvet, long-sleeved, full-length jumpsuit, was sold for US$153.50 {{stala|3541}} while the second, a long-sleeved, full-length blue and black patterned jumpsuit, was sold for US$410.65. {{stala|7755}} The jumpsuit was also worn by background actress [[Susan Lewis]] on ''Deep Space Nine'' as indicated by a costume tag. In his review of "Tribunal", author and screenwriter Dale Kutzera thought the character of Makbar, "''not only makes a weak Cardassian, but runs counter to the races previously all-male hierarchy.''" (''[[Cinefantastique]]'', Vol 26 #1, p.111) === Apocrypha === In the ''[[Star Trek: Typhon Pact]]'' {{novel}} ''[[Raise the Dawn]]'', set after the [[Dominion War]], Makbar presides over the trial of Denison Morad, who has destroyed a Federation industrial replicator in [[Lakat]]. Makbar, a member of the [[True Way]], is lenient towards Morad and sentences him to just one hundred days in the [[Hutet labor camp]], with the intention of recruiting him into the group when he is released. Makbar is also featured in the ''[[Star Trek Customizable Card Game]]''. === External link === * {{mbeta}} [[de:Makbar]] [[Category:Cardassians]] [[Category:Cardassian government officials]]

'''Tumek''' was a [[Klingon]] male, and the most trusted adviser to [[Grilka]].

He officiated at Grilka's and [[Quark]]'s [[brek'tal ritual]]. He along with Quark help her retain her house and standing in the [[Klingon Empire]] when her husband, [[Kozak]], was accidentally killed. 

When he and Grilka visited [[Deep Space 9]], he discouraged [[Worf]] from courting Grilka. Tumek said that since [[Worf]] was [[dishonor]]ed among [[Klingon]]s, Grilka could never mate with him. Tumek insulted him by telling him that he had become too accustomed to [[Human]] ways and knew nothing about how to pursue a Klingon woman. ({{DS9|The House of Quark|Looking for par'Mach in All the Wrong Places}})

{{bginfo|Tumek was played by ''[[Star Trek]]'' regular [[Joseph Ruskin]]. Tumek was the first character he had played in the modern ''Trek'' series and the only one to make more than one appearance.}}

[[Commander]] '''Kolana''' was a [[female]] [[Klingon]] [[warrior]]. She served as [[tactical officer|weapons officer]] [[commanding officer|under]] [[General]] [[Martok]] aboard the {{IKS|Ch'Tang}} in [[2375]]. 

She had the [[honor]] to serve with [[Dahar Master|''Dahar'' Master]] [[Kor]] in his final mission. Awed at first by the legendary warrior, she turned on him after his wits failed him in the [[raid on Trelka V]]. Kor won back her respect by sacrificing himself in battle with the [[Jem'Hadar]]. '''Ulani Belor''' was a [[Cardassian]] [[subspace]] [[scientist|researcher]] who worked for the [[Cardassian Science Ministry]] in the late-[[24th century]].

In [[2371]], she was sent to [[Deep Space 9]] as an academic associate of [[Gilora Rejal]], where they were to assist the [[Federation]] in their plans to install a [[subspace relay]] at the [[Gamma Quadrant]] entrance to the [[Bajoran wormhole]]. Unknown to her, she was part of a delegation that [[Yarka]], a former [[Bajoran]] [[Vedek]], believed was the fulfillment of [[Trakor's Third Prophecy]] and that the [[Celestial Temple]] would be destroyed. Belor worked with the DS9 crew and was successful, but only after [[Benjamin Sisko]] and [[Kira Nerys]] averted disaster from a [[rogue comet]]. ({{DS9|Destiny}})

{{bginfo|Belor was played by [[Wendy Robie]].|According to the script, the pronunciation of Belor's first name is "oo-LAH-nee." Furthermore, she is described as "''a pleasant and attractive woman.''" ''{{st-minutiae|resources/scripts/461.txt}}''|}}

'''Ortikan''' was a member of the [[Klingon Defense Force]] in the [[24th century]]. In [[2373]], he was serving on the {{IKS|Rotarran}} with his ''[[par'Mach'kai]]'', [[Tavana]].

When [[Jadzia Dax]] came aboard, she threw Ortikan from his seat in the [[mess hall]] to gain the recognition of the other [[Klingon]]s. 

After [[Kornan]] attacked [[Leskit]] in a [[drunk]]en rage, Ortikan tried to help, but was forced to the ground by Kornan. He began punching the younger Klingon with his fist until Dax shot Kornan with a [[phaser]], stunning him. Dax later took Ortikan to [[surgery]]. ({{DS9|Soldiers of the Empire}})

{{bginfo|Ortikan was played by stunt actor [[Scott Leva]].|The spelling of his name comes from the end credits of the episode. Some other sources like the script, the {{ste|4|2|115}}, or the cast list at [[StarTrek.com]] listing his name as "Ortakin". '''Tavana''' was a [[Klingon]] who served as the [[engineering officer]] on the {{IKS|Rotarran}} in [[2373]]. She was also the ''[[par'Mach'kai]]'' of her shipmate [[Ortikan]]. She befriended [[Jadzia Dax]] because [[Tavana's mother 001|her mother]] had previously met [[Curzon Dax]], though Jadzia impressed her in her own right. 

Her morale along with the rest of the [[crew]] was very low when Martok took over as [[commanding officer|commander]] of the ''Rotarran''. The [[ship]] had lost every battle in which it had fought the [[Dominion]]. The ''Rotarran'' was able to rescue the crew of the {{IKS|B'Moth}} and defeat the enemy, revitalizing the crew. Tavana and the rest of the crew of the ''Rotarran'' would become one of the best crews in the fight against the Dominion, and her ship became Martok's [[flagship]]. ({{DS9|Soldiers of the Empire}})

'''Torin''' was a [[Klingon]] {{dis|Guardian|Klingon}} in the [[24th century]] and member of the [[Followers of Kahless]]. 

In [[2369]], he participated in the creation of a [[clone]] of [[Kahless the Unforgettable|Kahless]]. When he "appeared" he helped to verify his story in the temple. Torin and Koroth later briefed the clone on the current political situation and tried to convince him to take over the [[Klingon Empire]]. When Worf challenged them on Kahless' status, he helped to explain what they did. ({{TNG|Rightful Heir}})

[[Genesis Lythe]] (adoptive sister) |actor = [[Karim Diané]] }} {{aquote|It is my honor to be present for the people I care about.|Jay-Den Kraag|3195|Ko'Zeine}} '''Jay-Den Kraag''' was a [[male]] [[Klingon]] [[Starfleet]] [[cadet]] in the [[32nd century]]. His name meant "he who crosses oceans of fire". == Early life == Hailing from the triad [[House of Kraag]], Jay-Den was the son of [[L'vanna]] and had two fathers, [[Drekol]] and [[Enok]]. Due to [[the Burn]] bringing the [[Klingon]]s to the brink of extinction, his family were refugees. Jay-Den's parents would sing Jay-Den and his older brother [[Thar]] to sleep with the myths of [[Kahless the Unforgettable]] at the [[refugee camp]]s which gave them comfort. By the time Jay-Den was nearing adulthood, his family resided on [[Krios Prime]]. While trading for a [[dermal regenerator]], Thar was stabbed with a poisoned weapon and died. While Jay-Den's family wanted him to become a true warrior and take his place in their House, Jay-Den dreamed of joining {{dis|Starfleet Academy|Earth}}, a dream that Thar had encouraged. Jay-Den's father Drekol held only disdain for the Federation and Starfleet and ordered him to kill a ''[[Veqlargh toQ]]'' to prove that he was a warrior as part of their family's rite of passage. Instead, Jay-Den chose to honor Thar by not killing the bird of prey. Jay-Den's father then shot at the bird and missed, and discarded the Starfleet transmitter with which Jay-Den and Thar had been listening to the broadcast from Starfleet Academy. Jay-Den's family left him to continue searching for a home while Jay-Den pursued his dreams with Starfleet. ({{SA|Vox In Excelso}}) == Starfleet Academy == [[File:Jay-Den Kraag personnel file.png|thumb|left|Jay-Den's cadet file]] A sciences major, he met Captain and Academy Chancellor [[Nahla Ake]], along with fellow cadet [[Caleb Mir]] on the {{USS|Athena}} prior to its arrival at [[San Francisco]], [[Earth]]. During an attack en route to Earth, he received his first field test of his skills having to perform a medical [[triage]] on [[Cadet Master]] and [[First Officer]] [[Lura Thok]]. ({{SA|Kids These Days}}) A strong association developed between him and Caleb at the start of the fall semester. ({{SA|Beta Test}}) Jay-Den was later informed that a Klingon refugee ship carrying his two fathers and his mother crashed on the way to [[Taurus VII]] and Jay-Den's family were feared to be amongst the casualties. Jay-Den insisted upon taking part in a series of debates overseen by [[the Doctor]] on the topic of the [[Klingon diaspora]] which led to an extremely heated debate between Jay-Den and Caleb on the subject. Jay-Den admitted to Thok that he felt that he had dishonored both worlds – Klingon and Starfleet – with his actions. However, Thok pointed out that Klingons did not miss out of rage. Instead, Thok believed that Drekol had missed his shot on purpose, thus honoring the hunt and Jay-Den's victory, letting his son go to pursue his dreams. Jay-Den was a Klingon warrior whose passion for death was only surpassed by his passion for life, who fought with words rather than weapons. With a new outlook, Jay-Den suggested a Klingon solution to the problem: meet the Houses in battle so that the Klingons could take their new homeworld through conquest as [[Kahless the Unforgettable]] did with [[Qo'noS]]. Starfleet and General [[Obel Wochak]]'s forces staged [[Battle of Faan Alpha|a battle]], allowing the Klingons to take their new homeworld as the spoils of war. Obel revealed to Jay-Den that his family had all survived and honored Jay-Den as a true Klingon warrior, gifting him with a ''[[HurwI']]'', a Klingon [[bow and arrow]]. Caleb repaired the transmitter that Thar had gifted Jay-Den who admitted that Caleb reminded him of his brother and the two made amends. ({{SA|Vox In Excelso}}) Jay-Den helped SAM with her attempt to solve the mystery of [[Benjamin Sisko]]. When told about Sisko's final confrontation with the [[Pah-wraith]]s, he was quick to assume that he was dead. Later, when SAM served her friends Sisko's legendary [[gumbo]], Jay-Den was eager to partake, even tasted the [[raktajino]] she had made just for him, only to admit that it had a horrendous taste, but thanked her for the effort. He then informed her of [[Jake Sisko]]'s unpublished novel called ''[[Anslem]]''. Much to Darem's frustration, Jay-Den remained on good terms with [[War College]] cadet [[Kyle Jokovich]] despite the rivalry between the schools. Kyle openly flirted with Jay-Den at [[The Academy]] bar and the two were shown dancing together. ({{SA|Series Acclimation Mil}}) Following the events on the {{USS|Miyazaki}}, Jay-Den and Kyle started dating and planned to spend their [[All-Worlds Day]] break together in [[Ibiza]]. However, when Darem was taken in a [[Khionian Marital Abduction]], Jay-Den followed him, mistakenly believing his friend to be in danger. The two argued about Darem getting married out of a sense of duty and Jay-Den stormed off, but returned to make a toast. Jay-Den's toast caused [[Kaira]] to realize that Darem was only marrying her out of obligation and the two got an annulment. Jay-Den and Darem shared a moment before he reunited with a sunburnt Kyle. ({{SA|Ko'Zeine}}) On the 300th night at the end of the academic year, Jay-Den invited his friends into the [[House of Kraag]] as his chosen family via the ''[[R'uustai]]'' rite which they accepted, although Caleb refused to drink. Jay-Den and [[Tarima Sadal]] later stowed away aboard the ''Athena'' to join an unauthorized mission to rescue their friends. Jay-Den defended his actions by telling Ake that Caleb was his chosen brother. Unable to beam them off of the ship, a frustrated Ake made the two wait in her office.
